title: The Last Calculation
dialogue: The office is already different. The spreadsheets are gone. The briefing documents are stacked in boxes. She is standing when you arrive.
monologue: She is standing. Elara sits for every meeting, every briefing, every argument. She sits because sitting is efficient and she is always efficient. She is standing because this is not a meeting.

narrative.text: I have been Finance Minister for thirty-one months. In that time I have managed three budget revisions, two currency stabilization interventions, and a debt restructuring that most economists said was impossible. I did all of it because I believed you were listening to the data even when you disagreed with my conclusions.

I told you eighteen months ago that overruling the Arcturian partnership would cost us international standing we could not afford to lose. The data was correct. The cost arrived on schedule. I have prepared a full transition briefing for my successor. It is on the desk.
She picks up her coat from the chair. The motion is the same precision she brings to everything — efficient, final, without drama.
I am not angry, Chancellor. I am a Finance Minister whose minister's advice was not followed. That is a data point. I am updating my model accordingly.

vostane_resignation_scene.monologue: She said she is not angry. She said it the way she says everything — as a statement of fact, not a performance. Elara Vostane is not angry. She is simply finished. The distinction is devastating.

choices.text: "I will not ask you to stay if the conditions that brought you here no longer exist. The transition briefing is thorough — I would expect nothing less. Thank you, Elara. For everything."
"Elara. I was wrong about the Arcturian decision. Tell me what you need from this government to stay and I will provide it."

narrative.text: Three things. Restore competitive bidding on the Arcturian technology contracts. Authorize the IMA review you declined eighteen months ago. And the next time I present data that contradicts your policy direction — you read it before you decide, not after.
She sets her coat back on the chair. She does not sit. But she does not leave.

choices.text: "Done. All three. I will have Vyktor arrange the Arcturian outreach by end of week."
"The IMA review and the Arcturian contracts — yes. The third condition I cannot accept as stated. I govern. I read the data. But the decision is mine."
